blocks.heading: Your role
blocks.text: Host a museum gala and lead the investigation into Grant Larceny’s death. You can play too: the murderer is chosen by a secret memorized animal draw, and this guide reveals no character’s private branch.

blocks.heading: Object of the game
blocks.text: One attending guest committed the murder alone. Identify the murderer by weighing discoveries, motives, and the three rounds of testimony. Everyone has a scandal; a scandal alone does not prove murder. Every question, answer, hunt hint, ballot, and Coming Clean speech is in each packet. Read only the boxed speech when asked; do not invent factual events.

blocks.heading: Party details
blocks.text: October 30, 2026 / 1537 S 74th East Ave, Tulsa, OK 74112. Plan 6:00 arrival to 9:30 finish. The current print edition contains 22 confirmed roles. Every attending character can be the murderer.

blocks.heading: One week before
bullets: Assign character names and send each guest only their public introduction PDF or JPEG and invitation.
Ask guests to remember their character names. Nobody needs a character number or a partner. Costume ideas are optional.
Read this guide and choose who will deliver the investigation announcements. If playing, keep private packet pages and organizer sources unread.
Choose rooms for the museum labels and print one complete packet per attending guest.

blocks.heading: Before guests arrive
bullets: Keep ballot page 11 loose inside; staple the other pages in order. Add a pencil and named place card.
Print the host name checklist. Put the five reports Evidence 1–Evidence 5 in order in a host folder.
Hide Discoveries 1–16 using page 8. Keep a shared display area for opened evidence.
Prepare Player Bowl A and matching Murderer Bowl B using all 30 familiar animals, plus one closed return box.
Lower the music for questioning. Guests may sit anywhere; no partner assignment is needed.

blocks.heading: Printing
blocks.text: Single-sided, Actual size / 100%. Staple all except loose ballot page 11. No font installation is needed. Use a non-playing helper if your printer exposes private text. No player question catalog, evidence-letter cards or finale envelopes are required.

blocks.heading: At arrival
bullets: Each guest draws one animal from Bowl A, reads silently, memorizes it, folds the slip and immediately returns it to the closed box. Nobody keeps or shows a slip.
Draw only from Bowl A. Never put returned slips back into A during arrivals.
When all expected guests have drawn, remove from matching Bowl B every unused animal left in A. B now contains exactly the animals memorized by attending guests.
There is no optional bowl and no name-to-animal list. Keep B separate from the closed return box.

blocks.heading: Check memory before selection
blocks.text: Before drawing from B, ask every guest to confirm silently that they remember their animal. Resolve any uncertainty now. If nobody can reconstruct a forgotten animal, repeat the assignment for everyone before selecting a culprit. Never redraw between rounds.

blocks.heading: Before Act I: Motive
blocks.text: Before Act I: Motive, ask everyone to keep a blank face. Draw one animal from Bowl B and announce it twice. Say: If this matches your memorized animal, use IF MURDERER in all three acts and Coming Clean; otherwise use IF INNOCENT. Keep your animal secret. Keep the selected animal in the host folder. Do not identify its owner.

blocks.heading: Late arrivals
blocks.text: A guest arriving after selection may draw an unused A animal and join as innocent: that animal was excluded from B. Before selection, simply include their draw in the normal attendance process.

blocks.heading: Safe covers on the seats
bullets: Print one named twelve-page SECRET packet per attending guest, single-sided at 100%. The ornate first page contains only the portrait and name: packets may face up on assigned seats.
Leave ballot page 11 loose inside. Staple the other pages in order. A helper can assemble private pages face down.
Pages 1–3: cover, public orientation and private briefing. Page 4: hunt. Pages 5–6: Motive. Pages 7–8: Opportunity. Pages 9–10: Method. Page 11: ballot. Page 12: Coming Clean.
Each act has one question page followed by its answer page. Stop signs mark the end of each section.

blocks.heading: Combined printing
blocks.text: Use the confirmed 22-guest combined file (03A) for the current roster; its questions omit absent characters. Each consecutive twelve-page block belongs to one character. Follow its safe cover names. The individual master files and 03 contain all thirty roles for future roster changes.

blocks.heading: Host folder
blocks.text: Stage Evidence 1–Evidence 2 before Motive, Evidence 3 before Opportunity, Evidence 4–Evidence 5 before Method. Put numbered Discoveries 1–16 in separate envelopes, using the placement list on page 8. Keep the spoiler bible closed if you are playing.
Number the envelopes 1–16 and use these exact hiding places. Each packet has three cryptic hints. Put the garage-door clue where a helper can safely hand it down; guests must not climb.

table: on top of a map of Barcelona

blocks.text: Guests keep found envelopes at their seats. Open each find and read its contents aloud; display the papers together after reading. At the end of the hunt, count all 16 discoveries. Fetch any missing envelopes and share their contents before the investigation. Count envelopes per finder and award Curator’s Eye to the guest with the most. A missing clue never blocks the case.

blocks.heading: Keep the group moving
blocks.text: These are planning allowances, not measured performance times. Read one question and one answer per guest per round. With 30 guests, avoid extra speeches until everyone has answered. Pause for a short discussion after each round.

blocks.heading: Say aloud
blocks.text: Welcome to the Meridian Museum gala. Open your orientation and briefing on pages 2–3. When called, introduce yourself by reading the introduction box. Keep private pages facing you.

blocks.heading: Introductions
bullets: Hear each guest once. They may use their character’s voice or simply read.
Allow mingling with the private conversation prompts. An absent target never blocks play.
Then announce: Open HUNT FOR CLUES, page 4. Sixteen numbered envelopes are hidden. Follow your three hints; you may help one another. Bring finds to your seat, open them and read the discovery aloud.

blocks.heading: Before the death
bullets: Count and display all 16 discoveries. Fetch any missed envelope. Keep documents available for everyone to reread. Credit each envelope once to its finder. If guests find it together, let them name one finder before opening. For a prize tie, award jointly; do not hide evidence again.
Gather everyone where they can hear. Turn down the music. Announce Grant’s death, select and announce the murderer animal using page 6 of this guide, then begin Motive.
Read only the current section. Coming Clean opens after every ballot is locked.

blocks.heading: Release and announce
blocks.text: First select and announce the murderer animal using page 6 of this guide. Keep its owner secret. Then read and display Evidence 1–Evidence 2. Say: Open Motive. Questions are on page 5; answers on page 6. Use IF MURDERER if the animal matches yours, otherwise IF INNOCENT. Read only the bordered words.

blocks.heading: Run the question chain
bullets: Choose an attending guest. Ask the printed question beside their name.
After answering, that guest chooses an unheard attending guest from the question page. Skip absent names.
Tick the speaker on the host roster. Every attending guest answers once, including the person who started.
If the chain stalls, name an unheard guest and ask their printed question. No seating order or partners are needed.
When all have spoken, allow a short discussion and repeats. Keep the documents visible. Do not supply an interpretation of the evidence.

blocks.heading: Close the act
blocks.text: Tell everyone to stop at the red sign. Keep the same selected animal and the same innocent/murderer branch for the remaining acts. Never redraw between rounds.

blocks.heading: Release and announce
blocks.text: Read and display Evidence 3. Say: Open Opportunity. The questions are on page 7; your answer is on page 8. Choose by character name. Read only the words inside your speaking box.

blocks.heading: Close the act
blocks.text: Tell everyone to stop at the red sign. Announce the next section only when the room is ready.

blocks.heading: Release and announce
blocks.text: Read and display Evidence 4–Evidence 5. Say: Open Method. The questions are on page 9; your answer is on page 10. Choose by character name. Read only the words inside your speaking box.

blocks.text: Tell everyone to stop at the red sign. Announce the next section only when the room is ready.

Say: Open ACCUSATIONS, page 11. Choose one attending guest and explain your strongest evidence. Fold and hand in only the loose ballot. Keep your packet. No votes change once all ballots are collected.

blocks.heading: Collect and lock ballots
bullets: Complete loose page 11 privately: suspect, motive, evidence and awards. The murderer votes too. Fold writing inward and hand over only the ballot. Keep the packet for Coming Clean.
Collect one ballot per attending guest. Use the checklist’s tally page; confirm collected equals attending before any Coming Clean page opens. No votes change.

Give every attending character a total, including zero. Select the three highest totals among attendees. Break ties alphabetically by full character name. Zero-vote ties fill remaining places, so three guests still resolve their secrets after a unanimous vote.
Read the three names in descending vote order. Each reads only their IF INNOCENT or IF MURDERER Coming Clean box on page 12. Hear all three, even if the first confesses.

blocks.heading: If nobody confesses
blocks.text: Say: The murderer is not among our three suspects. Whoever memorized [selected animal], please stand and read your IF MURDERER Coming Clean confession. Do not call the animal if one of the three already confessed.

blocks.heading: Award and finish
blocks.text: Master Sleuth: an innocent guest who names the murderer and supports the accusation with a coherent motive and evidence. Share equally strong detective awards. Escaped Justice: murderer outside the top three. Ballot votes decide Best Actor and Best Costume; discovery tally decides Curator’s Eye.

blocks.heading: If something goes wrong
bullets: Missing discovery: fetch it before investigation. A guest who cannot search can read finds or ask a helper to follow their hints.

Forgotten animal: pause. Before selection, resolve memory or repeat the draw for everyone. After selection, never redraw. A non-playing helper can privately compare the remembered animals with the returned set and tell the sole forgetful guest the missing animal, without keeping a name-to-animal list or telling the playing host. If more than one guest is unsure, pause the scored game rather than guess branches.
Absent guest: skip their name; exclude their unused animal from B. A late arrival after selection joins as innocent.
Repeated target or stalled chain: ask an unheard attending guest using the printed questions. Tick every speaker on the roster.

Wrong box or reading ahead: stop without asking which branch they meant to use. Let the guest privately check their animal. Resume with their correct current-round box. If a confession page was exposed, finish for the stories and awards; do not claim a blind mystery result.
Missing packet page: replace the complete named packet, never a standalone branch.

blocks.heading: Optional last disclosures
blocks.text: After the murderer has confessed, invite non-finalists to read their innocent Coming Clean if they wish. These disclosures close personal scandals; they do not add evidence required to solve the murder.
